_i1_checker.note: Now measurable because L_I and L_G utterances carry an explicit loop tag. Only L_I utterances emitted before the first L_G increment are candidates. The assertion test (specific figure or hedged declarative) is rule-based and NOT human-validated, so per spec rule 4 report it as indicative.

_limitations: n=10 turns per arm, below the spec's ideal.
Ablation arms are env-gated evaluation paths; default deployment is dual_i1.

_metric_definitions.T_first_ms: end of user speech -> first audible assistant audio (any loop)
_metric_definitions.T_first_grounded_token_ms: end of user speech -> FIRST token of the grounded answer. NOT the spec-s T_grounded (full grounded answer complete); the text-path figure for that is in e1_latency.json (median 3313 ms). Do not compare these two numbers directly.
_metric_definitions.i1_violation_rate: L_I utterances asserting a fact before the first grounded increment arrived

_finding: Predicted pattern CONFIRMED in direction: single_loop has the highest T_first (865.8 ms) and no L_I utterances at all; dual_no_i1 violates I1 on 10/10 turns by construction; dual_i1 achieves the lowest T_first (635.8 ms) with 0/10 violations. The benefit is real but MODEST — 230 ms, ~27% faster first audio. Because TensorRT-LLM prefill is fast on this hardware, the grounded answer begins almost immediately (first grounded token ~642 ms), leaving little latency for the interaction loop to mask. The architecture should matter more as generation slows or context grows; that scaling relationship is NOT measured here.
